scope.description: One command with a value of 70000 bytes marshalled and unmarshalled through the real codec, on a deployment whose client command size is configurable (aws.conf sets 1000).
assumptions: the client's command size is a configuration value, so larger values are constructible
the codec is the only framing between a client or peer and the replica's readers
excluded: the default deployment's 1000-byte commands, which are inside the field's range
what a replica does after its reader desynchronises on the following message

properties.reason: Independent applicability, correlated prerequisites and fully observed result comparison

adaptations: harness-only scaffolding: no replica is constructed; the test calls the state codec directly on a buffer holding two commands
two commands in one buffer model a batch or a recorder that appends commands, which is how the implementation writes them

plan_uncertainties: the check does not attach the shifted stream to a replica reader, so the reader's own reaction is unobserved
the shipped configuration's 1000-byte commands never reach the boundary
grounding_unresolved: whether the client refuses oversized commands before sending (client/buffer.go allocates the configured size, which the read did not check for a cap)
the durable recorder's own append order is a separate observation
